chapter: Jump for Joy, records and royalties
title: Free-lance recording for every label and being underpaid
summary: Back in New York he recorded for Decca and many others as a free-lancer, but was badly paid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, I was little and cute then. As the cats say, I was ready. Put on anything, it look good. And we got together, I met a who-o-o-ole lotta chicks out here, and then I went to work after the show closed. I went back to New York City. Again, I started workin' ...I made some records...started makin' records with Decca...made some records with Decca. In fact, I made some records with every company I ever heard of. Me, I just sung...I've been on so many labels I don't know what labels I ain't been on. Some of these new ones I ain't been on but all them records back then there was...I had a ball. I was makin' records for ever'ybody. I wouldn't sign no contract with nobody. I say, "I'm free-lance. If you want me to sing, I'll do a session for you. Just pay me. I'll do it."
They were robbin' me. I didn't know how much money you were supposed to get. I just workin' for little or nothin'. I just so glad to make a records.
You ever get any royalties on any of those records?
I'm drawin' a royalty right today.
